It's mostly a list of British folk rock, almost exclusively traditional songs in 60/70s electric arrangements.

Fairport Convention (they created British electric folk, together with Pentangle):

  • Matty Groves (obviously)
  • Tam Lin (well, obvously too)
  • Sailor's Life
  • Crazy Man Michael - basically the whole Liege & Lief album is a very, very solid piece of folk

Pentangle:

  • The Cuckoo
  • Hunting Song (grooveshark link) + live version
  • Dragonfly
  • Let No Man Steal Your Thyme (grooveshark link) + live - that double bass :)
  • Yarrow - if you like this, definitely check another version by Shelagh McDonald, which I posted below

Sandy Denny (!!! - don't expect me to be unbiased here, I love her voice (well, she also sung in Fairport)):

  • Late November (grooveshark link) (not strictly folk, but I have to always post it) + live video on youtube
  • Who Knows Where The Time Goes (her only hit single - with Fairport, but written long before that)
  • Fhir A Bhata (her first recording, quite charming)
  • 3:10 To Yuma
  • The North Star Grassman And The Ravens (grooveshark link) (from the album with the same title, Late November is from there too, I enjoy the nostalgic atmosphere/feel this album gives me - its cover perfectly matches the music)
  • Ecoute, Ecoute

Steeleye Span (electric folk classic):

  • Cam Ye O'er Frae France
  • Edwin
  • King Henry
  • Gaudete (grooveshark link) (not really folk, but interesting)

Incredible String Band (they fall into the weird/electric folk category):

  • Dear Old Battlefield
  • Koeeoadi There

Mellow Candle (Irish prog-folk, they released only one LP in early 70s, but damn, it was good):

  • Heaven Heath
  • Boulders On My Grave

Anne Briggs (classic folk, no electric stuff, "just" singing):

  • Let No Man Steal Your Thyme (grooveshark link)
  • Blackwaterside (grooveshark link)

Trees (Psychedelic electric folk) * Murdoch * Lady Margaret * Garden of Jane Delawney

Shelagh McDonald (another amazing voice, not better than Sandy, but great):

  • Dowie Dens Of Yarrow
  • Stargazer
  • Odyssey (not strictly folk, but I like it)

Marianne Faithfull - not a folk singer, but I like her version:

  • Scarborough Fair
